currentConcept.role: current concept: identify a base word and suffix in three-sound closed-syllable words with -s and -es
currentConcept.notes: Introductory and ongoing concept. Students read the word without the suffix first, then the whole word with the suffix.

currentConcept.role: current concept: read/spell suffix -s as /s/ or /z/ and suffix -es as /ĭz/
currentConcept.notes: The source models -s in shops and bugs and -es in mixes, wishes, and tosses.

currentConcept.role: subsequent concept: distinguish plural nouns from action verbs formed with -s/-es
currentConcept.notes: The Step Instruction labels plural nouns versus action verbs as Subsequent Lessons.

sourceOrderedTeachingSequence.notes: No new letter-sounds. Introduce base word/suffix and -s/-es sounds first; plural noun versus action verb is subsequent instruction. Real-word accuracy/automaticity precedes 1.6 nonsense-word reading.
Use the blank yellow suffix tile. For spelling, students name and spell the base word first and then add the suffix. Plural versus action verb spelling is subsequent instruction.

soundInventoryRefs.role: all previously taught vowel Letter-Sound Cards plus selected previously taught consonant and welded sounds
soundInventoryRefs.notes: The Step Instruction explicitly states there are no new letter-sounds in 1.6.

wordElementRefs.role: current taught Word Element Cards for suffix -s and suffix -es

hfwRefs.locator: PDF-p-20 / printed-p-16 and PDF-pp-27-28 / printed-pp-23-24: they, have, one, from, both

reviewPoolRefs.role: actual previous-Substep controlled review pool for 3-4 prior words
source-valid current real-word and nonsense-word reading pools

reviewPoolRefs.notes: The Step Instruction says students should become accurate and automatic with 1.6 real words before doing nonsense words.

selectionRules: Drill all previously taught vowel Letter-Sound Cards.
Be selective with previously taught consonant and welded cards.
There are no new letter-sounds in 1.6.

contentRefs.role: Introductory and ongoing reading instruction for base word plus suffix -s/-es
Subsequent reading instruction distinguishing plural nouns from action verbs

selectionRules: Begin with 3-4 actual 1.5 review words.
For initial 1.6 instruction, teach the base-word/suffix concept and the /s/, /z/, and /ĭz/ suffix pronunciations.
Students read the base word first, then the whole word with the suffix.
Do not pull plural-noun versus action-verb instruction forward before the introductory suffix work is established.

contentRefs.role: current Word Card routine, suffix-sound sorting, and later plural/action sorting

selectionRules: Begin with the existing previous-Substep fat stack.
For current 1.6 Word Cards, have the student read the base word first and then the whole word.
Use taught -s/-es Word Element Cards separately as needed.
Review the current 1.6 HFW set plus prior unmastered HFWs.

contentRefs.role: Part 4 practice/charting procedure and real-before-nonsense boundary

selectionRules: Practice with 5-6 words from one current-substep list reflecting the day's instruction.
For charting, use another current-substep list reflecting the day's instruction and have the student read 15 words.
Students read the base word first and then the suffixed word.
Establish accuracy and automaticity with 1.6 real words before moving to 1.6 nonsense words.
Use the exact current sentence page reflecting instruction and embed all 10 sentences.
Weave questions about base word/suffix, suffix sound, current and previous concepts, vocabulary/meaning, and phrasing.

contentRefs.role: Quick Drill in Reverse and suffix-tile preparation

selectionRules: Use selected previously taught vowel, consonant, and welded phonemes.
Add the blank yellow suffix tile for the Part 7 spelling work.
After -s and -es are taught, include selected taught suffix elements as needed.

contentRefs.role: Introductory and ongoing spelling of base words plus -s/-es

selectionRules: Begin with 3-4 actual 1.5 words.
Students name and spell the base word first and then add the suffix.
Use the blank yellow Suffix Tile for -s/-es and mark the base word/suffix as directed.
Keep plural-noun versus action-verb spelling for Subsequent Lessons.

contentRefs.locator: words+nonsense: PDF-p-18 / printed-p-14; phrases: PDF-p-20 / printed-p-16; sentences: PDF-pp-27-28 / printed-pp-23-24

contentRefs.role: Written Work Dictation direction and base-word/suffix marking

selectionRules: Use source-verified Dictation Book items for current 1.6 real words, nonsense words, HFW phrases, and sentences.
When dictating suffixed words, have the student repeat the whole word, name/spell the base word first, then add the suffix.
Underline the base word and circle the suffix; circle HFWs and scoop phrases/sentences as appropriate.
